title: Russia says its pullout from Gori is complete while Georgia and the West dispute it
body:
On 22 August 2008 Russia announced that its pullout from Georgian territory was finished, with the statement given at 15:50 GMT by General Nikolai Uvarov. Uvarov said at least 40 Russian military vehicles had left Gori heading north toward Russia and that full removal would take longer because of the volume of troops and a single road and tunnel. Al Jazeera's Jonah Hull reported a large convoy of troops and armour leaving Gori and Georgian police preparing to enter the city.

Georgia disputed the claim. Shota Utiashvili of the interior ministry said the withdrawal was not complete and that Russian presence in Senaki and Poti was illegal. Reports described Russian soldiers digging trenches near Poti. The Pentagon saw "no clear sign" of substantial withdrawal, the White House said Russia had not fully left undisputed Georgian territory, and British Foreign Secretary David Miliband said he was deeply concerned that forces had not returned to pre-fighting positions.

Russia said about 500 peacekeepers would remain in a buffer zone around South Ossetia. A map shown by General Anatoly Nogovitsyn included a Russian zone of responsibility covering much of the road from Poti to Senaki. Under the ceasefire, Russia could keep a security zone extending 7 km into Georgia from South Ossetia. At the UN, the United States, France and Britain demanded immediate withdrawal, while Russia proposed a resolution restating the six-point peace plan.
